chunks: Your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) for nearly two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or one-third of it, and a group of those with you. And Allah determines the night and the day. He knew that you would not be able to calculate it perfectly, so He turned in mercy to you. So recite what is easy for you of the Qur'an.
He knew that there would be among you the sick, and others traveling through the earth seeking from His bounty, and others fighting in the cause of Allah. So recite what is easy of it for you.

And establish prayer, and give zakat, and lend Allah a goodly loan. And whatever good you put forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah; it is better and greater in reward. And seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the duration of night prayer in Islam?
ai.summary: This verse (73:20) serves as the final abrogation of the strict night prayer obligation in Surah al-Muzzammil, transitioning the community from intense individual devotion to a balanced practice accommodating the practical realities of sickness, travel, and jihad. Shia scholars highlight this concession as a manifestation of divine mercy (rahmah), ensuring that worship remains sustainable and inclusive for all believers regardless of their physical or circumstantial state. It effectively links the spiritual discipline of Tahajjud with the communal pillars of Salah, Zakat, and charitable giving, emphasizing that ease in worship does not diminish its reward.
